title: fix(plugin-auth)!: accepting, declining and listing an invitation need a verified email address on every deployment
body:
Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no skill under `skills/**` teaches accepting an organization invitation or invitation sign-up; `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx` gains the rules in this change.

ADR amendment: #34909, lands with this PR.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：接受、拒绝邀请和列出自己的邀请，在每个部署上都要求会话的邮箱已验证（403，better-auth 自己的码），与邮件能否投递无关；按 id 读取单个邀请（get-invitation）保持开放。`invite_only` 下凭邀请 id 注册的账号，邮箱验证前不加入组织，验证后接受邀请时按邀请的角色入组。控制台：接受、拒绝被拒，以及凭邀请链接注册后自动接受被拒，都直接转到验证邮件页。
- 为什么改：邀请 id（邮件链接和复制链接都带）不能证明持有受邀邮箱；按维护者的裁决，规则对所有部署无条件成立。
- 风险与回滚：BREAKING。没有可投递邮件的部署不能再让密码账号靠邀请链接入组（社交或 SSO 已验证邮箱的账号除外），改由平台管理员建号或用 Add Member 挂接已有账号。本 PR 还更正了同一版本里 #34666 尚未发布的 changeset（见下方 DELIBERATE CORRECTION），Check Changeset 因此按设计保持红色。回滚即 revert 本 PR 与 #34909。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-accept-verified-email.ts`（规则与两个 vendor 钩子）；`auth-manager-membership-admission.ts` 的 `settleMembership`（未验证的邀请注册不绑定，按创建它的请求判断）；`packages/verify/src/harness.ts` 的 `signUp`（测试夹具改走运营方通道）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/invitation-acceptance-verified-address.test.ts`，预期 30 个用例全绿。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地（ADR 修订 #34909 按 Tier H 由你批准，与本 PR 一同落地）。

## DELIBERATE CORRECTION

This PR rewrites `.changeset/34272-accept-invitation-verified-email.md`, the pending release note of #34666, which exists on the merge base. The rule this PR ships made that note's sentences about deployments without live mail, and about listing and declining, false; left as it was, the release would carry two contradictory BREAKING entries for one route. `check-empty-changeset` stays red on this file by design; it is not restored. The note is reduced to the parts that ship beside this PR's entry and points at that entry, which carries the BREAKING notice and the migration.

| Part of the note | Before | After |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Summary line | "fix(plugin-auth,app-shell)!: while mail is live, accepting an invitation needs a verified address" | "fix(plugin-auth,app-shell): an accept refused for an unverified address answers the vendor's own code, and the Console's accept page takes the person to verify" |
| Clause-② line | "Clause-②: no (narrowing)" | "Clause-②: no" |
| Skills-docs line | "…; the rule is stated here and in the self-hosting docs." | "…; the rule is stated in the self-hosting docs." |
| ADR-0087 disposition marker (an HTML-comment line beginning `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`) | present | removed: the note no longer declares a breaking change |
| BREAKING paragraph | "**BREAKING** for a person who accepts an invitation from an account whose address was never verified, on a deployment whose mail transport is live. The rule: while mail is live, accepting an invitation needs a verified address, because an unverified address is not proof of the invited mailbox." | "The rule that refuses the accept is stated, with its BREAKING notice and its migration, in this release's entry "accepting, declining and listing an organization invitation need a verified email address on every deployment, and an invitation sign-up joins by accepting once verified". This entry carries only the parts of that change that ship beside it." |
| What changes, first bullet | "`POST /api/v1/auth/organization/accept-invitation` (`@objectstack/plugin-auth`), from a session whose address is unverified, while the email service answers `isConfigured() === true`, now answers `403 EMAIL_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED_BEFORE_ACCEPTING_OR_REJECTING_INVITATION` (better-auth's own code and sentence, the ones its accept route answers when its option is on) and writes nothing; the invitation stays pending. It used to answer `200` and write the membership. The vendor's not-found, expiry and recipient refusals still come first, so a session that is not the invitee learns nothing new. The check runs on the vendor's `beforeAcceptInvitation` hook, on the session user the vendor itself resolved (cookie or bearer token alike), and asks whether mail is live on every request." | "`POST /api/v1/auth/organization/accept-invitation` (`@objectstack/plugin-auth`) answers a session whose address is unverified with better-auth's own `403 EMAIL_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED_BEFORE_ACCEPTING_OR_REJECTING_INVITATION` and its sentence, the answer its accept route gives when its option is on, and writes nothing. The vendor's not-found, expiry and recipient refusals still come first, so a session that is not the invitee learns nothing new. The check runs on the vendor's `beforeAcceptInvitation` hook, on the session user the vendor itself resolved (cookie or bearer token alike)." |
| What changes, second bullet (the Console) | unchanged | unchanged |
| Who moves paragraph | "**Who moves.** A person in that state verifies their address … so is refused as above and sent to verify." | removed; this PR's entry states who moves and what to do |
| Unchanged paragraph | "**Unchanged.** Every deployment without a live mail transport (no email service, or the log transport), where nothing could verify an address, so acceptance stays open to an unverified address; `get-invitation`, `list-user-invitations` and `reject-invitation`, which write no membership; the one-step door …; and a verified session everywhere. better-auth's `requireEmailVerificationOnInvitation` stays declared `false`: it governs reading and declining too, and is read once at boot." | removed; this PR's entry states what is unchanged |
| `@objectstack/runtime` line | unchanged | unchanged |

## What changes

**The rule.** Accepting, declining and listing an organization invitation need a verified email address, on every deployment, whatever the state of its mail transport. Reading one invitation by its id stays open, so the accept page can show it. A password account verifies through the verification mail; an account a social or SSO provider made counts only when the provider verified the address. The invitation's id, which its accept link and a copied link carry, is no proof of the mailbox, and no setting relaxes the rule.

- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-accept-verified-email.ts`: `refuseUnverifiedInvitationAnswer(user, { verificationRequired })` refuses a user whose address is not verified with the vendor's own `403 EMAIL_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED_BEFORE_ACCEPTING_OR_REJECTING_INVITATION` (read off the plugin's `$ERROR_CODES`; the local fallback is pinned equal to it). It reads no mail state.
- `auth-manager-organization-plugin.ts`: the rule is asked from better-auth's `beforeAcceptInvitation` and `beforeRejectInvitation`, which the vendor fires after its own not-found, expiry and recipient checks and before anything is written, with the session user its own verification check reads (cookie and bearer alike). `requireEmailVerificationOnInvitation` stays declared `false`: the vendor's option governs accept, reject and get-invitation together, and get-invitation stays open.
- `list-user-invitations-verification.ts`: the host's rebuild of `GET /organization/list-user-invitations` refuses a session whose address is not verified, `403 EMAIL_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED_FOR_INVITATION`, unconditionally, so the inbox carries the rule itself whatever the declaration says. The listing itself stays the vendor's own query.
- **Mail state.** No invitation gate reads whether mail is live, so every transport state (live, log transport, no email service, a service whose liveness cannot be read or whose reader throws) gives the same answer.
- **Invitation sign-ups.** Under `invite_only` with `membershipPolicy: 'auto'`, a sign-up admitted by the invitation it presents is not bound to the deployment's organization while its address is unverified (`settleMembership`, `auth-manager-membership-admission.ts`). The admission gate records the admission on the request that creates the account, and both settle seams of that creation read it there; no other creation of the same address, in any other request, can read it. It joins by accepting the invitation once verified, with the invitation's role, or through a platform administrator. Chosen as a policy-skip at creation rather than a bind at verification: the invitation is the instrument of admission under this posture and its acceptance already writes the membership; a role-less bind at verification would let a verified person who never accepted, or who declined, join by a route no issuer chose; and ADR-0093 D7 decides membership at creation, where a verification-time bind would add a decision point on every path that can write `email_verified`. A user row that cannot be read while that request admitted an invitation sign-up binds nothing. The first account, accounts an administrator creates, accounts a boot command provisions and a sign-up the invitation mail's proof verifies bind as before.
- **Console** (`@object-ui/app-shell`): the accept page answers a refused decline with the verification-mail screen for the account's address, as it answers a refused accept; and a sign-up from an invitation link (`useInvitationSignUpJoin`) whose automatic accept is refused for an unverified address goes straight to that screen, whose link returns to the accept page, instead of passing through the accept page first. The Console has no caller of the listing route.
- **Fixtures.** Fixture members enter through the operator door instead of the invitation sign-up lane: `operatorProvisioningField` in plugin-auth's `audience-gate-test-support.ts` (three suites), `@objectstack/verify`'s `signUp` (which falls back to the invitation lane only when the auth service offers no operator door), and four `@objectstack/runtime` pin suites. Fixtures that answer an invitation mark the invitee verified first.
- **Docs.** `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx` states the rule and its consequence: a deployment without a live mail transport cannot onboard a password account by invitation link; an invitee whose social or SSO provider verifies the address can still accept a copied link there; otherwise a platform administrator creates the account, or attaches an existing one with **Add Member**, which is open to platform administrators only and attaches existing accounts only. `tenancy-modes.mdx`, `environment-variables.mdx`, `permissions/authentication.mdx` and `permissions/sso.mdx` state the sign-up binding rule and that admission is not acceptance. `docs/qa/platform-checklist/RUNNER.md`'s persona door 1 follows the rule. `ui/.../invitationSignUpJoin.ts`'s header describes the flow. `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs`: one comment sentence.
- **Changesets.** `.changeset/invitation-acceptance-verified-address.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/verify`, `@object-ui/app-shell` patch; BREAKING; `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. `@object-ui/console` is not listed: no file under `ui/apps/console` changes, and the `@object-ui/*` and `@objectstack/*` packages version as one fixed group. `.changeset/34272-accept-invitation-verified-email.md`: the DELIBERATE CORRECTION above.

No spec, schema, stored row, route path, error code or exported signature of a published entry changes.

## Tests

- `src/invitation-acceptance-verified-address.test.ts` (real `AuthManager` over `@objectstack/driver-sql` on sqlite `:memory:`), 30 cases:
  - an unverified password account and an unverified provider-asserted social account are refused at accept, decline and the listing, the one-step door asks them to verify, and get-invitation answers; verified controls accept and decline (password through the real verification mail round trip; social with a provider-verified address); the one-step door accepts with the mail's proof and, for a signed-in account, once the address is verified;
  - the mail-transport matrix: live, log transport, no email service, a service with no liveness reader, a service whose reader throws, each for an unverified password account, an unverified social account and a verified control;
  - the binding cases: an unverified invitation sign-up holds no membership and its session no active organization; verifying binds nothing by itself and accepting writes the invited role; the same with no mail transport; controls: a proof-verified sign-up invited into another organization holds the default-organization membership from creation and the invited role from acceptance; an unrelated address an operator provisions while an invitation sign-up is in flight is bound; the same address created again through the operator door after an invitation sign-up of it is bound; the first account is bound.
- `src/invitation-accept-verified-email.test.ts`: the vendor's own code; accept and decline refused for cookie and bearer sessions with nothing written; get-invitation open; the vendor's recipient refusal still answers first at both doors; verified controls; the one-step proof door; the function's pins.
- `src/list-user-invitations-verification.test.ts`: the listing refuses an unverified session while get-invitation answers; scope pins on a verified session; the rebuild's contract and the vendor pin.
- UI: `acceptInvitationVerifiedEmail-34272.test.tsx` (a refused decline goes to the verification-mail screen, beside the accept case and its control); `invitationSignUpJoin-30125.test.tsx` (an unverified invitation sign-up goes straight to the verification-mail screen with its address and the accept page as the return).

## Acceptance notes

- ADR amendment: #34909 (docs/adr, Tier H), lands with this PR.
- The no-mail invite outcome messages that still name Copy Invite Link as the hand-over are follow-up card #34889 (seat-filed).
- A follow-up owned by the seat extends the rule to the `email_domain` posture.
- `AuthManager.isEmailDeliveryLive` is unchanged: its remaining readers (the existing-address sign-up answer, the invite's delivery outcome, `features.emailDelivery`, the visitor verification resend) back success claims, where an unreadable transport reading as not live is the honest direction. No invitation gate reads it.
- `@objectstack/verify`'s `signUp` keeps its invitation-lane helper as the fallback; the helper is also a control of `check:swallow-census-controls`, which is why it stays.
- Governed paths: none in this PR. The ADR amendment is in #34909.
